questions.question: A man purchases a certain number of identical calculators at a rate of ₹1,200 per dozen. He sells them at ₹110 per piece. Find how many calculators he bought if his total profit is ₹360.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit per **dozen** = (**Selling Price** per piece × 12) − **Cost Price** per dozen

⇒ Profit per dozen = (110 × 12) − 1200 = 1320 − 1200 = ₹120

Total items in **dozens** = **Total Profit** ÷ Profit per dozen = 360 ÷ 120 = 3 **dozens**

Total number of **calculators** = 3 × 12 = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36 calculators.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Cost Price** (CP) of 1 dozen (12 calculators) = ₹1,200

**Selling Price** (SP) of 1 calculator = ₹110

**Total Profit** = ₹360

**Formula Used:**

1. **Profit** per unit = **Selling Price** per unit − **Cost Price** per unit

2. Number of units = **Total Profit** ÷ **Profit** per unit

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/11aba4b9e43b74c680f3faac83e09dc66e913855d6745a8ad88038d3ae70391d.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ **Cost Price** (CP) of 1 calculator = 1200 ÷ 12 = ₹100

⇒ **Selling Price** (SP) of 1 calculator = ₹110

⇒ **Profit** on 1 calculator = 110 − 100 = ₹10

⇒ Number of **calculators** bought = 360 ÷ 10

⇒ Number of **calculators** = 36

**∴ The correct answer is 36 calculators.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit Percentage Formula

Profit % = (Profit ÷ **Cost Price**) × 100. In this case, Profit % = (10 ÷ 100) × 100 = 10%.

Selling Price Calculation

SP = CP × (100 + Profit %) ÷ 100. This is used to find the **Selling Price** when CP and profit percentage are known.

Unitary Method in Profit and Loss

Always convert given quantities (like dozens, gross, or score) into **single units** to simplify the calculation of profit or loss per item.

questions.question: A metal sphere is dropped into a cylindrical container of diameter 20 cm partially filled with water. If the water rises by 1.5 cm, what is the radius of the sphere?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of **sphere** = Volume of **water displaced** in the cylindrical container.

(4/3) × r³ = R² × h (Since π cancels out from both sides)

(4/3) × r³ = 10² × 1.5

r³ = (150 × 3) ÷ 4 = 112.5

r = √³(112.5) ≈ 4.8 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 4.8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the **cylindrical container** = 20 cm

Rise in the **water level (h)** = 1.5 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of **Cylinder** = πR²h

Volume of **Sphere** = (4/3)πr³

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b2e1b1dc2db0d7ecf724821a1b451c8c26af4b8dd0f421025c9485426e96f862.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Radius of cylinder (R) = 20 ÷ 2 = 10 cm

⇒ Volume of water raised = Volume of cylinder with height 1.5 cm

⇒ Volume of water raised = π × (10)² × 1.5

⇒ Volume of water raised = 150π cm³

⇒ According to **Archimedes' Principle**, Volume of sphere = Volume of displaced water

⇒ (4/3) × π × r³ = 150π

⇒ 4 × r³ = 150 × 3

⇒ 4 × r³ = 450

⇒ r³ = 450 ÷ 4 = 112.5

⇒ r = √³(112.5)

⇒ r ≈ 4.827 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 4.8 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Archimedes' Principle

When an object is fully or partially submerged in a fluid, the volume of the **fluid displaced** is equal to the volume of the **submerged part** of the object.

Volume of a Sphere

The volume (V) of a sphere with radius (r) is given by the formula V = (4/3)πr³. The **surface area** is 4πr².

Volume of a Cylinder

The volume (V) of a cylinder with base radius (R) and height (h) is V = πR²h. The **curved surface area** is 2πRh.</p

questions.question: The marked price of a cupboard is ₹3,200, which is 25% above the cost price. It is sold at a discount of 10% on the marked price. Find the profit percentage.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked price of cupboard = ₹3,200

Marked price is 25% above cost price.

Discount on marked price = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Cost price = Marked price ÷ (1 + Markup percentage)

Selling price = Marked price × (1 - Discount percentage)

Profit percentage = [(Selling price - Cost price) ÷ Cost price] × 100

questions.question: A quality control officer tracks the defect rates in 4 different machines in a textile factory. The first machine produces fabrics with an average defect rate of 1.8%, the second with 2.4%, and the third with 1.6%. The fourth machine operated for 5 fewer hours than the average runtime of the first three, yet its total defective output was 0.92 units. If the total number of defective units from all four machines is 4.12, and each machine's total production was identical, find the defect percentage of the fourth machine.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Defect rate₁ = 1.8%

Defect rate₂ = 2.4%

Defect rate₃ = 1.6%

Total defective units (all 4) = 4.12

Defective units of 4th machine = 0.92

Total production of each machine = same

**Formula Used:**

Defective units = Production × Defect% ÷ 100

Total defective = Sum of individual defectives

**Calculation:**

⇒ Defective units from first three = 4.12 − 0.92

⇒ Defective units from first three = 3.20

⇒ Let production of each machine = P

⇒ P × (1.8 + 2.4 + 1.6) ÷ 100 = 3.20

⇒ P × 5.8 ÷ 100 = 3.20

⇒ P = 3.20 × 100 ÷ 5.8

⇒ P = 320 ÷ 5.8

⇒ P = 55.1724

⇒ Defect% of 4th = 0.92 × 100 ÷ 55.1724

⇒ Defect% of 4th ≈ 1.67%

**∴ The correct answer is approximately 1.67%.**

questions.question: A, B, and C invest ₹20,000, ₹30,000, and ₹50,000, respectively, in a business. The profit at the end of the year is ₹50,000. What is A's share of the profit?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A's investment = ₹20,000

B's investment = ₹30,000

C's investment = ₹50,000

Total profit = ₹50,000

**Formula Used:**

Profit share ratio = Investment of A : Investment of B : Investment of C

Individual share of profit = (Individual ratio × Total profit) ÷ Total ratio

**Calculation:**

⇒ Profit share ratio = 20,000 : 30,000 : 50,000

⇒ Profit share ratio = 2 : 3 : 5

⇒ Total ratio = 2 + 3 + 5 = 10

⇒ A's share of profit = (2 × 50,000) ÷ 10

⇒ A's share of profit = 100,000 ÷ 10

⇒ A's share of profit = ₹10,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10,000.**

questions.question: A ladder rests against a vertical wall and makes an angle theta with the horizontal ground such that tan theta = 5/12. If the length of the ladder is 13 meters, find the height at which the ladder touches the wall.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

tanθ = 5 ÷ 12

Length of ladder = 13 m

**Formula Used:**

tanθ = Perpendicular ÷ Base

Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

**Calculation:**

⇒ Perpendicular : Base = 5 : 12

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(5² + 12²)

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(25 + 144)

⇒ Hypotenuse = √169 = 13

⇒ Scale factor = 13 ÷ 13 = 1

⇒ Height = 5 × 1 = 5 m

**∴ The correct answer is 5 m.**

questions.question: A sum of Rs. 6,400 amounts to Rs. 8,100 in 8 years at a certain rate of interest, compounded annually. Find the amount received after 4 years when Rs. 2,240 are invested at same rate of compound interest (compounded annually).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal₁ = 6400

Amount₁ after 8 years = 8100

Time₁ = 8 years

Principal₂ = 2240

Time₂ = 4 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount = Principal × (1 + r)ⁿ

**Calculation:**

⇒ 8100 = 6400 × (1 + r)⁸

⇒ (1 + r)⁸ = 8100 ÷ 6400

⇒ (1 + r)⁸ = 81 ÷ 64

⇒ (1 + r) = (81 ÷ 64)¹ ÷ ⁸

⇒ 81 = 3⁴ and 64 = 2⁶

⇒ (81 ÷ 64)¹ ÷ ⁸ = (3⁴ ÷ 2⁶)¹ ÷ ⁸

⇒ (1 + r) = 3¹ ÷ ² ÷ 2³ ÷ ⁴

⇒ (1 + r)⁴ = (81 ÷ 64)¹ ÷ ²

⇒ (1 + r)⁴ = 9 ÷ 8

⇒ Required amount = 2240 × 9 ÷ 8

⇒ Required amount = 2240 × 1.125

⇒ Required amount = 2520

**∴ The correct answer is 2520.**

questions.question: The ratio between the son and mother is 1:3. After five years, the ratio of their age becomes 3:7. What are the ages of the son and mother?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Ratio of son and mother's age = 1:3

After 5 years, ratio of their age = 3:7

**Formula Used:**

Present age = Ratio constant × Ratio value

Future age = Present age + 5

**Calculation:**

Let the present ages of son and mother be 1x and 3x respectively.

After 5 years:

⇒ (1x + 5) ÷ (3x + 5) = 3 ÷ 7

Cross multiplying:

⇒ 7(1x + 5) = 3(3x + 5)

⇒ 7x + 35 = 9x + 15

⇒ 35 - 15 = 9x - 7x

⇒ 20 = 2x

⇒ x = 10

Son's age = 1x = 10

Mother's age = 3x = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 10, 30.**

questions.question: In a circle, chord AB subtends an angle of 75° at the circumference at point C. A tangent is drawn at point A. If the angle between this tangent and chord AC is 40°, what is the measure of the angle subtended by the minor arc AC at the center of the circle?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

∠ACB = 75°

Angle between tangent at A and chord AC = 40°

**Formula Used:**

Angle between tangent and chord = Angle in opposite arc

Angle at center = 2 × Angle at circumference

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/eb8eba01452b6e012755ae4db36e1af8333056e0a22338295f47edf5dab07ee5.png] 

⇒ Angle between tangent and chord AC = Angle in opposite arc

⇒ ∠ABC = 40°

⇒ In △ABC:

⇒ ∠BAC = 180° − (75° + 40°)

⇒ ∠BAC = 180° − 115°

⇒ ∠BAC = 65°

⇒ Minor arc AC subtends ∠ABC at circumference

⇒ ∠ABC = 40°

⇒ Angle at center = 2 × 40°

⇒ Angle at center = 80°

**∴ The correct answer is 80°.**

questions.question: A car and a bus travel at speeds in the ratio of 5:3. The bus covers a distance of 360 km in 6 hours. What is the time taken by the car to cover the same distance?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed ratio (Car : Bus) = 5 : 3

Distance = 360 km

Time taken by bus = 6 hours

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Speed of bus = 360 ÷ 6

⇒ Speed of bus = 60 km/hour

⇒ 3 parts = 60

⇒ 1 part = 20

⇒ Speed of car = 5 × 20

⇒ Speed of car = 100 km/hour

⇒ Time taken by car = 360 ÷ 100

⇒ Time taken by car = 3.6 hours

**∴ The correct answer is 3.6 hours.**

questions.question: In a class, ratio of the boys to the girls is 5:3. If 20% of the boys and 40% of the girls fail an exam, what is the ratio of the number of boys who passed to the number of girls who passed?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Pass % of **boys** = 100% − 20% = 80%

Pass % of **girls** = 100% − 40% = 60%

Required **Ratio** = (5 × 80%) : (3 × 60%)

⇒ 400 : 180 = 20 : 9

**∴ The correct answer is 20:9.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of **Boys** : **Girls** = 5 : 3

Fail % of **Boys** = 20% | Fail % of **Girls** = 40%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/21f55ac531c8487a10b355d44965b30dbbaa6c5a451ab4e3ee798a5981c7368b.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the number of **boys** be 500 and **girls** be 300.

⇒ Number of **boys who passed** = 80% of 500

⇒ Passed boys = (80 ÷ 100) × 500 = 400

⇒ Number of **girls who passed** = 60% of 300

⇒ Passed girls = (60 ÷ 100) × 300 = 180

⇒ Required **Ratio** = 400 : 180

⇒ Divide both by 20: (400 ÷ 20) : (180 ÷ 20) = 20 : 9

**∴ The correct answer is 20:9.**

**__Additional Information__**

Complementary Percentages

The sum of **passing percentage** and **failing percentage** is always 100%. If x% fail, then (100 − x)% pass.

Ratio Scaling Property

Multiplying or dividing both terms of a **ratio** by the same non-zero constant (e.g., multiplying 5:3 by 100 to get 500:300) does not change the value of the ratio.

Base of Percentage

Always ensure the **percentage** is applied to the correct base. Here, 20% is of boys (5 units) and 40% is of girls (3 units).</p

questions.question: If sec(theta)=cosec(42°), what is the value of theta?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

sec(theta) = csc(42^circ)

**Formula Used:**

sectheta = (1)/(costheta)

cscalpha = (1)/(sinalpha)

sin(90^circ - alpha) = cosalpha

**Calculation:**

⇒ (1)/(costheta) = (1)/(sin42^circ)

⇒ costheta = sin42^circ

⇒ sin42^circ = cos(90^circ - 42^circ)

⇒ sin42^circ = cos48^circ

⇒ costheta = cos48^circ

⇒ theta = 48^circ

**∴ The correct answer is theta = 48^circ.**

questions.question: A trapezoid is formed by cutting a smaller triangle from the top of a larger similar triangle. If the height of the smaller triangle is (1)/(3) of the height of the larger triangle, what is the ratio of the area of the trapezoid to the area of the larger triangle?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **heights** of smaller triangle to larger triangle = 1 : 3.

Ratio of their **areas** = (1)² : (3)² = 1 : 9.

Area of the **trapezoid** = Area of larger triangle − Area of smaller triangle = 9 − 1 = 8 units.

Required **ratio** = Area of trapezoid : Area of larger triangle = 8 : 9.

**∴ The correct answer is 8:9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Height of **smaller triangle** (h) = 1/3 × Height of **larger triangle** (H)

⇒ h/H = 1/3

**Formula Used:**

For two **similar triangles**, the ratio of their **areas** is equal to the square of the ratio of their corresponding **heights** or **sides**.

⇒ Areaₛₘₐₗₗ / Areaₗₐᵣgₑ = (h/H)²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c8bd06944001076349ee6ce5025144764dd6db57c5bbe63a920a8477783530d1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Areaₛₘₐₗₗ / Areaₗₐᵣgₑ = (1/3)²

⇒ Areaₛₘₐₗₗ / Areaₗₐᵣgₑ = 1/9

⇒ Areaₛₘₐₗₗ = (1/9) × Areaₗₐᵣgₑ

⇒ Areaₜᵣₐₚₑzₒᵢd = Areaₗₐᵣgₑ − Areaₛₘₐₗₗ

⇒ Areaₜᵣₐₚₑzₒᵢd = Areaₗₐᵣgₑ − (1/9) × Areaₗₐᵣgₑ

⇒ Areaₜᵣₐₚₑzₒᵢd = (8/9) × Areaₗₐᵣgₑ

⇒ Areaₜᵣₐₚₑzₒᵢd / Areaₗₐᵣgₑ = 8/9

**∴ The correct answer is 8:9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Similarity Property of Areas

If two triangles are similar, the ratio of their areas is equal to the square of the ratio of any two corresponding linear dimensions (sides, medians, altitudes, or perimeters).

Area of a Trapezoid

The area of a trapezoid formed by a parallel cut in a triangle can always be calculated as the difference between the areas of the original triangle and the smaller triangle removed from the top.

Midsegment Theorem Case

If the cut is made at the midpoints (h = 1/2 H), the area of the smaller triangle is 1/4 of the larger, and the trapezoid is 3/4 of the larger triangle area.</p
